suggestion.title: SMS Phishing — Fake Messaging App Support Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'fake support texts' used to steal credentials. Pipeline did not surface this initial access vector despite being central to the headline and kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound SMS containing messaging app service names (Telegram, Signal, Viber, WhatsApp) combined with urgency language (verify identity, confirm account, reset password). Flag SMS from numbers inconsistent with known carrier/app vendor profiles. Cross-correlate timestamp with subsequent authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing — Messaging App Account Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials were 'stolen'; pipeline ignored the downstream attack—credential validation/reuse. Critical for detecting account compromise post-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid failed login attempts to messaging platforms (Telegram, Signal) within minutes of SMS phishing delivery, followed by successful authentication from new device/IP. Alert on credential reuse across multiple apps if user was targeted.

suggestion.title: Session Hijacking — Unusual Login Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After credentials stolen via phishing, attacker would log in remotely. Pipeline missed this post-compromise detection opportunity mentioned implicitly by 'steal messaging credentials'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag messaging app logins from geolocation inconsistent with user baseline (e.g., Ukraine user, sudden login from Russia/proxy). Alert on concurrent sessions from multiple IPs. Monitor for contact list exfiltration or message forwarding rules post-login.

suggestion.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass — Post-Phishing Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Successful credential theft despite MFA is a sophisticated indicator. Article implies success; detection should monitor for MFA circumvention or app-specific bypass (recovery codes, backup codes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests for MFA reset, recovery codes, or backup authentication methods within 1 hour of phishing SMS. Alert on successful authentication without MFA challenge if MFA is normally enforced. Monitor for 'lost authenticator' scenarios that coincide with credential phishing.

suggestion.title: Contact List Exfiltration — Lateral Target Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Ukraine as victim. Stolen messaging credentials expose contact lists; this is standard post-compromise lateral targeting. Pipeline ignored data collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk contact/roster exports or automated sync requests immediately after account compromise. Alert on export of Ukrainian government, military, or critical infrastructure personnel from compromised accounts. Track subsequent phishing campaigns targeting those exported contacts.

suggestion.title: Russian State Actor — SMS Phishing Campaign Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Russian Intelligence' conducted operation. Pipeline extracted zero threat-actor context. FSB, GRU, or SVR TTPs include SMS phishing and credential targeting of strategic targets (Ukraine). Attribution required for strategic intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference SMS phishing campaigns targeting Ukrainian officials/infrastructure with known Russian state actor tooling (SIM-swapping infrastructure, credential harvesting frameworks). Correlate timing with geopolitical events. Flag if SMS originates from compromised carriers or proxy SMS gateways attributed to Russia.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'Deploys Cobalt Strike'—the most critical observable is C2 beacon activity, yet no command-and-control detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS POST requests to known Cobalt Strike C2 domains or characteristic beacon patterns (regular interval POST, specific User-Agent spoofing). Detect DNS queries to attacker-controlled infrastructure followed by suspicious encrypted sessions.

suggestion.title: SharkLoader Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces SharkLoader as the initial payload vehicle but pipeline generated no process-execution detection for the loader itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known SharkLoader variants by hash or behavioral signature. Monitor for suspicious script-based execution (PowerShell, cmd.exe with encoded args) spawning secondary payloads or network communication.

suggestion.title: Process Injection for Cobalt Strike Implant
suggestion.rationale: Cobalt Strike payload delivery typically involves process injection (T1055), a core evasion technique absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect code injection into system processes (svchost, lsass, explorer) via suspicious memory access patterns. Monitor for process hollowing: legitimate parent spawning child with unusual memory allocation or early termination followed by remote access.

suggestion.title: Malware File Staging and Download
suggestion.rationale: Deployment of SharkLoader implies initial download/staging phase, but no file-transfer or ingress detection was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of unknown executables to temp directories (%TEMP%, %AppData%\Local\Temp) followed by execution. Monitor for file creation from untrusted sources or suspicious email attachment execution.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Binary (LOTL) Abuse for Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Malware campaigns routinely abuse legitimate tools to evade detection; no LOTL-focused detection was generated despite being a known defense-evasion pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of system binaries (regsvcs, mshta, certutil, rundll32) with unusual parent-child relationships or network-connected behavior. Monitor for encoded/obfuscated command-line arguments and suspicious registry modifications related to malware execution.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Process Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'host code execution' as impact. Should detect when AI agent runtime (Python, Node.js, etc.) spawns command shells or system binaries post-web-request.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation from known AI agent processes with suspicious parent-child relationships. Correlate timing to web page fetch/parsing events. Flag shell invocations, script interpreter calls, or system binary execution from agent processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from AI Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: Web-page-based attack implies agent fetches remote content or exfiltrates data. Should monitor for unusual outbound connections from agent processes to untrusted/non-whitelisted domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor all network connections originating from AI agent processes. Flag non-whitelisted destinations, suspicious port/protocol combinations, and patterns consistent with C2 or payload staging.

suggestion.title: Process Injection or Suspicious DLL Load by AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: 'Hijack' language in title suggests process manipulation or code injection. Should detect cross-process writes, DLL injection attempts, or module loading anomalies initiated by agent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process injection patterns (WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread) or suspicious module loads (unsigned DLLs, search-order hijacking) originating from or targeting AI agent processes. Correlate to web-request timeline.

suggestion.title: Exploit Indicators in Web Content Served to AI Agent
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'one web page'—must detect when HTML/JavaScript payloads target agent parsing. Should identify embedded exploit patterns, script tags with suspicious attributes, or encoded payloads in HTTP responses consumed by agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP responses destined for or originating from AI agent processes. Flag HTML containing embedded script tags with obfuscation, iframe loading from suspicious sources, or JavaScript payloads known to exploit parsing vulnerabilities.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Memory Access Patterns in AI Agent Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Web-page hijacking likely requires memory corruption or runtime manipulation. Should detect unusual heap operations, buffer operations, or memory writes in agent process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor memory operations (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory) targeting or originating from AI agent processes. Flag patterns consistent with shellcode injection, ROP gadget chains, or heap spraying.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens or headers. Splunk: `index=_internal source=*web.log* uri=*sidecar* status=200 | search NOT auth_token=*`. KQL: `DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort in (5432, 8000, 8089) and RemoteIPType == 'Public' and InitiatingProcessName contains 'splunk'`.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—post-exploitation impact. File truncation (size=0) initiated by service processes outside maintenance windows is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file truncation (size=0) or bulk deletion initiated by splunkd or sidecar processes targeting paths outside $SPLUNK_HOME. Splunk: `sourcetype=syslog (action=delete OR action=truncate) file_size=0 process=splunkd* | stats count by file_name, process`. KQL: `FileDeleteEvents | where InitiatingProcessName contains 'splunkd' and TargetFilePath !contains 'SPLUNK_HOME'`.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Unpatched Splunk Enterprise Asset Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV standard asset-exposure hunt. Article specifies federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21—unpatched or late-patched instances represent exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scans for Splunk Enterprise with CVE-2026-20253 unpatched or patched after 2026-06-21. Cross-reference with network exposure (public IPs, internet-facing services). Splunk: `search CVE=CVE-2026-20253 NOT patched | table host, ip, splunk_version, last_scan_date`. KQL: `DeviceInfo | where ProductName contains 'Splunk' | join (SecurityUpdate | where CVE=='CVE-2026-20253' and UpdateStatus!='Installed')`.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Exposure Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sidecar endpoint is network-reachable; missing authentication means ports (5432 or custom sidecar service port) are accessible to unauthenticated remote users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful connections to port 5432 or Splunk sidecar service ports from non-RFC1918 address ranges. Splunk: `sourcetype=firewall dest_port=5432 src_ip NOT CIDR(10.0.0.0/8) NOT CIDR(172.16.0.0/12) NOT CIDR(192.168.0.0/16) connection=accepted | stats count by src_ip, dest_ip`. KQL: `DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemotePort==5432 and RemoteIPType=='Public' and InitiatingProcessName contains 'splunk'`.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — need detection for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints lacking authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk web server and sidecar service logs for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints (paths: /services/sidecar, /_sidecar, pgbouncer admin interface) originating from untrusted IPs or lacking Authorization/session headers. Baseline authenticated traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' — pipeline should generate detection ensuring scanners identify vulnerable Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners detect CVE-2026-20253 on any Splunk Enterprise asset. Cross-reference against federal patch due date (2026-06-21) and escalate unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack enables 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — need file-system detection for unexpected file operations sourced from sidecar process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation, truncation, and deletion events where source process is PostgreSQL sidecar (pgbouncer, postgres wrapper) or where files in Splunk directories (etc/, var/lib/, var/log/) are modified via API without corresponding administrative action logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Web Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild — require asset-exposure hunt to locate publicly-reachable Splunk instances vulnerable to this unauthenticated endpoint attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances with web interface accessible from Internet (port 8000, 8089) or via DNS. Cross-check patch status and alert on unpatched instances found externally-facing; remediation priority given federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Sidecar PostgreSQL API Requests Modifying Data Without Auth Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically in 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — need detection for API calls that execute file operations without authentication validation in request context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sidecar API logs for POST/PUT/DELETE requests to file-operation endpoints lacking authentication headers, JWT tokens, or session tokens. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or requests from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—core exploitation path. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically /_sidecar or /services/sidecar patterns) that complete without successful authentication. Baseline legitimate sidecar traffic first; alert on anomalous request patterns from external sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation in Splunk Application Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'create...arbitrary files'—a direct impact indicator. Zero file-creation detection use cases in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation events within /opt/splunk and /splunk-data directories, particularly files created by the Splunk user context outside normal installation/update operations. Correlate with unauthenticated web access logs from same source IP/timeframe.

suggestion.title: File Truncation and Data Destruction via Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'truncate arbitrary files' capability—destructive impact indicator. Pipeline generated no detection for file deletion or truncation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file deletion or truncation events (zero-byte rewrites) in Splunk directories and dependent data stores. Alert if correlation shows delete/truncate events preceded by unauthenticated HTTP requests within 30 seconds. Compare against maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT Requests to Sidecar File Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file creation/truncation 'through...endpoint'—implies HTTP parameter passing to trigger file operations. No HTTP payload analysis use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST/PUT requests to sidecar endpoints containing file operation parameters (e.g., 'file=', 'path=', 'truncate='). Alert on requests that include file paths pointing to /opt/splunk or sensitive directories. Baseline legitimate sidecar API calls first.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article directly names CVE-2026-20253 as the vulnerability in Splunk Enterprise; CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation. Baseline detection is CVE matching against scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Splunk Enterprise hosts reporting CVE-2026-20253. Cross-check against patch deployment logs and asset inventory to identify unpatched instances. Prioritize internet-facing instances and those accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack vector explicitly: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to PostgreSQL sidecar service ports on Splunk Enterprise hosts for requests lacking authentication tokens or credentials. Flag HTTP/TCP connections that return success status codes without prior login sequence. Correlate request timing with file-operation anomalies on the Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Splunk Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and MITRE T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Detection requires identifying Splunk instances exposed to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CSPM tools for public IPs bound to Splunk-tagged instances. Search network telemetry for inbound connections to Splunk default ports (8089, 8000) or sidecar service ports from external/untrusted source IPs. Cross-reference with Shodan/Censys for externally-indexed Splunk instances.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File truncation is the impact signature of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk host filesystems for file truncation operations (size reduction to zero, delete syscalls, SetFilePointer calls) especially in config, log, or data directories. Correlate timing with sidecar process spawning or unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests. Alert on mass truncation events within a short window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Database Integrity Compromise
suggestion.rationale: PostgreSQL is Splunk's backing data store; truncating DB files indicates evidence destruction or data corruption. Article's 'truncate arbitrary files' capability directly applies to *.db and backup files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL data directory (/var/lib/pgsql or configured path) for unexpected truncations to *.db, *.log, or backup files. Flag TRUNCATE/DELETE commands issued via PostgreSQL wire protocol without audit-trail credentials. Alert on sudden drops in Splunk audit log volume or missing audit records post-intrusion.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Publicly Accessible Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability against 'public-facing application'—detection of exposed Splunk instances is the prerequisite exploit condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8089, 8000) responding to unauthenticated requests or without authentication enforcement. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 scanner results. Any exposed instance with unconfirmed patch status is exploitable per CISA KEV timeline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability mechanism is 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the execution vector and should be hunted directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint for HTTP requests lacking valid authentication headers or session tokens. Red flags: HTTP 200/201 responses to sidecar without prior authentication, unauthenticated requests from external IP ranges, or 401→200 sequences indicating auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct file destruction is the impact action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file truncate/create operations initiated by Splunk service accounts or PostgreSQL processes. High-fidelity indicators: truncation of Splunk configuration files, data directories, or critical system files. Establish baseline of legitimate backup/rotation activity and exclude.

suggestion.title: HTTP-Based Exploitation of CVE-2026-20253 (File Manipulation Payloads)
suggestion.rationale: Sidecar endpoint is HTTP-accessible per article. Exploitation requires POST/PUT requests with file path or truncation directives, detectable at HTTP layer pre-impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/PUT requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints containing file path parameters, truncation directives, or SQL injection patterns. Escalate if correlated with missing Authentication header, lack of established session, or requests from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can reach the endpoint; detection should surface requests lacking auth headers or failed-auth sequences prior to file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/API requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths (typically :8089 or internal HTTP) that lack Authorization headers, or show repeated 401s followed by successful requests. Look for User-Agent or request patterns consistent with curl/automated tools.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation/Truncation Following Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files'; file system events coinciding with endpoint access indicate exploitation success. Phrase: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation in unexpected directories (e.g., /tmp, config, logs, app directories) on Splunk hosts within 1–5 minutes of unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access. Flag writes to sensitive Splunk paths (bin, etc).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context ('actively exploited') implies attackers are finding exposed Splunk instances; detection of reconnaissance toward sidecar endpoint is early indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of HTTP requests targeting known PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths (e.g., /api/sidecar, /postgres/*, /db/*) with 404/401 responses or timeouts, originating from external IPs to Splunk web ports.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due-date context + T1190 tag establish public-facing app; SOC must identify which Splunk instances are internet-reachable and prioritize.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk Enterprise instances with public IPs or DNS records pointing to internet-facing addresses. Cross-check against security.properties version info and patch status (6.4.x before patch XYZ, 9.x before patch ABC, per vendor advisory once released).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Abnormal Process or Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation via sidecar endpoint implies out-of-band process spawning or database queries; abnormal sidecar behavior post-access is indicator of successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process for unusual child processes (shell, python, perl), unexpected network connections from sidecar to external IPs, or SQL statements modifying non-standard tables post-unauthenticated endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—detecting exposure of this service is the asset-exposure baseline article references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service on expected ports from untrusted/external sources. Look for successful TCP handshakes to the service endpoint lacking standard SQL authentication.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Critical Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core trait: 'missing authentication for critical function'—detection must flag attempts to invoke protected functions without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls to Splunk critical functions (file creation/truncation endpoints) lacking valid authentication headers or with invalid/missing credentials. CVE-2026-20253 specifically allows unauthenticated exploitation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Splunk Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Attack impact explicitly: 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files'—impact detection must monitor for suspicious file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation, modification, or deletion originating from Splunk Enterprise processes or via the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint, particularly outside maintenance windows. Correlate with unauthenticated endpoint access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature
suggestion.rationale: KEV entry indicates active exploitation—specific CVE detection is standard for known-exploited vulnerabilities with federal remediation deadlines (due 2026-06-21).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk service endpoints matching CVE-2026-20253 exploitation patterns: unauthenticated requests to PostgreSQL sidecar, file-manipulation function invocations without valid tokens.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise — Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct evidence of exploitation vector. Zero use cases generated despite this attack path being the core vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated requests (no auth token / session) to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints. Baseline legitimate tool access, then flag external IPs or automation tools without credentials attempting sidecar operations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise — Suspicious File Creation via PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — impacts are file operations, not code execution. No use case captures file-system IOCs from this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/truncation events spawned by Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar process (running as splunk user or postgres-sidecar role). Flag creation of files outside expected Splunk directories or system-critical paths (e.g., /etc, /var/log).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise — CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies active exploitation against exposed instances. Article URL points to federal remediation mandate but no use case for identifying vulnerable Splunk instances in your fleet (version scanning or banner enumeration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal and DMZ networks for Splunk Enterprise instances running versions ≤9.0.x (affected range per CVE). Cross-correlate with patch inventory to identify unpatched assets. Prioritize publicly routable instances or those accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise — Exploitation Attempt via Unauthenticated Sidecar Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific attack flow: unauthenticated → sidecar endpoint → file operations. Detection should directly map that sequence to identify exploitation attempts in access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints with HTTP 200/201 responses that lack valid authentication headers (no Authorization, Session-ID, or Bearer token). Correlate with subsequent file write syscalls in that time window.

suggestion.title: HTTP 200 on Protected DotVVM Endpoint Without Authorization Header
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'AuthorizeActionFilter simply does nothing, no hacking is needed to bypass the filter.' The exploitation is unauthorized access. No UC detects successful access to protected endpoints. Behavioral exploitation signature is entirely missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP logs for requests to endpoints decorated with [Authorize] or similar protection attributes that return HTTP 200 when Authorization header is missing, malformed, or contains invalid token. Baseline: such endpoints should reject (401/403) unauthenticated requests. Flag sudden success-rate increase on protected endpoints.

suggestion.title: DotVVM Protected Resource Access Without Session Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workaround: 'use AuthorizeAttribute instead,' implying protected resources exist in DotVVM apps. Exploitation succeeds by simply omitting auth proof. No detection for unauthenticated successful access to sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to DotVVM application sensitive endpoints (/admin, /api/*, /data/export, /sensitive/*) that return HTTP 200 when session/auth cookies are absent or invalid. Correlation with vulnerable version inventory. Track source IPs, request paths, response codes for anomaly detection.

suggestion.title: Spike in Anonymous Access to Protected DotVVM Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability allows unauthenticated users to access protected resources without error. No anomaly detection for sudden increase in successful-access patterns to endpoints that should require authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For hosts running vulnerable DotVVM versions: establish baseline of authenticated vs. unauthenticated request ratio to protected endpoints. Flag rapid increase in HTTP 200 responses to protected paths from unauthenticated sessions (missing/invalid tokens). Compare 7-day trend against 30-day baseline.

suggestion.title: Internet-exposed Splunk Enterprise inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article frames this as a public-facing application vulnerability (T1190); CISA KEV entry signals active exploitation. Core hunt: 'Asset: [CVE]: asset-exposure hunt — canonical Splunk SPL template'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk instances on public internet or DMZ via shodan/censys queries, DNS records, and vulnerability scanner results. suggestion.title: Unauthenticated requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Sidecar is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints (e.g., localhost:8077 or cluster-peer ports) for absence of Authentication/Authorization headers or token validation. Flag successful (200–201) responses to file-operation requests from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Anomalous file creation/truncation by Splunk process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Detect file operations outside normal Splunk data directories (e.g., system /etc, /var, application configs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on splunkd/splunk-otel processes creating or truncating files in restricted paths (/etc, /var, /opt outside Splunk dirs). Baseline normal file I/O patterns and flag bulk deletes, mass creations to atypical directories, or writes to system-critical paths.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise version detection and patch-gap analysis
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV includes federal due date 2026-06-21. Rapid version enumeration is mandatory. Article specifies 'Splunk Enterprise' product and vulnerable-version range (implicit via CVE-2026-20253).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning for Splunk Enterprise version. Correlate against CVE-2026-20253 affected versions. Compute days-since-patch and alert on instances >90 days unpatched. Track patch deployment lag against federal due date.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL sidecar anomalous queries or file operations
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits sidecar service for file manipulation. Detect abnormal query patterns or file-system operations initiated via sidecar from non-Splunk processes or external origins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sidecar logs for file operations (CREATE, TRUNCATE, unlink) from untrusted source IPs or non-splunkd processes. Flag queries originating outside Splunk cluster or from unexpected client libraries.

suggestion.title: Authentication bypass attempts on Splunk sidecar endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access is the core vulnerability vector. Reconnaissance phase will probe for endpoints and auth weaknesses, leaving detectable traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal auth-failure rates on sidecar endpoints. Alert on spikes in 401/403 errors, NULL auth headers, or invalid token attempts. Correlate auth-failure patterns with successful sidecar access to detect two-stage attacks: probe → exploit.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack surface: 'missing authentication for critical function' via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk instances targeting the PostgreSQL sidecar (typical port 5432 or custom variants) that lack authentication headers, valid session tokens, or originate from unexpected sources. Baseline legitimate postgres connections and correlate anomalies against vulnerability scanner data to identify exploitation attempts against unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Unauthenticated Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the post-authentication impact phase enabling log destruction or system tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or deletion initiated by Splunk processes or the postgresql sidecar service, especially in sensitive directories (Splunk/etc, Splunk/var/log, certificate stores). Alert on unexpected removal of configuration or audit log files that could disable security controls or hide attacker activity.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Splunk Enterprise Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation indicates active in-the-wild exploitation; enterprise patch lag is common. Article establishes federal remediation due-date (2026-06-21) as compliance driver; network-facing instances without compensating controls require immediate identification.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposed Instance Detection & Version Scanning
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly requires fleet-wide patch verification (due date 2026-06-21). Pipeline produced no asset-discovery or version-scanning use case for identifying vulnerable Splunk instances on the perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for internet-facing Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089, 9997). Enumerate version strings via /en-US/api/apps or /services/server/info endpoints. Cross-reference against patched version timeline and flag instances older than vendor remediation for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface but pipeline omitted reconnaissance/discovery phase. Attackers typically probe endpoint before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or probe attempts targeting Splunk sidecar ports (8191 or custom PostgreSQL ports) from external sources. Look for TCP SYN scans, service banner grabbing attempts, or connection probes to non-standard PostgreSQL ports on Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can access the sidecar service endpoint; this is the primary attack surface and should be detected via lack of authentication headers/tokens in requests to the sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise HTTP endpoints for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar paths (typically /_sidecar/* or /postgres/*) that lack valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Baseline legitimate sidecar access and alert on anomalous unauthenticated patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to... truncate arbitrary files' — this is file-delete activity through a sidecar service and should be detected via file operation logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file deletion/truncation events where the initiating process is Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service. Flag deletion of configuration files, application binaries, or data directories initiated from sidecar context with no corresponding user/admin action.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'create... arbitrary files' through the sidecar — complement file truncation detection with file creation detection to catch both write and delete attack patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation events initiated by Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service. Alert on creation of executables, config files, or suspicious paths in system directories or Splunk's application tree initiated through the sidecar rather than normal Splunk processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific CVE identifier (CVE-2026-20253) with federal patch due date; standard practice is to hunt for active exploitation attempts matching known attack signatures or patterns for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query web logs and proxy telemetry for requests containing CVE-2026-20253 exploitation patterns or known PoC signatures targeting Splunk Enterprise. Correlate with instances not patched by 2026-06-21 federal deadline to identify unpatched exposures.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV represents active exploitation; standard practice is to verify Splunk Enterprise instances are not exposed without authentication and are running patched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk Enterprise asset inventory for instances without authentication enabled, exposed on public/DMZ networks, or running versions prior to the patch release date. Cross-reference with active web telemetry to confirm which exposed instances have received exploitation probes.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the attack surface and must be monitored for intrusion attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/TCP requests to known Splunk sidecar service endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens. Flag POST requests from external IP ranges attempting to interact with file-operation endpoints. Baseline legitimate sidecar traffic and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Monitor Suspicious File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability enables attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—directly observable file-system behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, modification, or truncation events where Splunk sidecar is the parent process, particularly outside standard Splunk data/log directories. Truncation to zero-bytes should trigger immediate investigation. Correlate with sidecar endpoint access logs.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Scan: Splunk Enterprise with Internet-Facing Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation; the sidecar endpoint must be internet-reachable. Identify and patch all exposed instances before 2026-06-21 federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20253 matches. Cross-reference with IP reputation databases and external ASN logs to confirm sidecar endpoint exposure. Prioritize unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances reachable from public networks or WANs.

suggestion.title: Detect Audit Log Destruction via Sidecar File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation capability (stated in article) is a post-exploitation defense-evasion vector if used against audit logs to cover attack tracks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexplained gaps, zero-byte files, or missing entries. Correlate file-truncation events on audit log paths with sidecar endpoint access logs. Alert on any file-destruction operations initiated via the vulnerable endpoint.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit vector is 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—pipeline missed this as the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials. Focus on POST/PUT operations to internal service ports (typically 8191-8199 range for Splunk sidecars) originating from untrusted source IPs or user agents consistent with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article's core impact statement: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—detection of file operations in this context is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, modification, or deletion events initiated by Splunk service accounts (splunkd, postgres sidecar runner) targeting files outside expected $SPLUNK_HOME/var or /etc/splunk directories. Flag rapid file truncations (zero-byte writes) as potential evidence destruction.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access via internal 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this suggests service-to-service or lateral-movement detection is needed if endpoint is compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which internal hosts legitimately communicate with Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar. Alert on new source IPs, unexpected protocols, or external traffic attempting to reach this internal service endpoint. Investigate failed authentication attempts followed by successful access.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Tampering via Sidecar Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Ability to 'truncate arbitrary files' through sidecar implies potential for config destruction or persistence via Splunk's configuration layer—'truncate' specifically suggests evidence elimination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexplained file modifications to $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/ subdirectories (app.conf, props.conf, transforms.conf). Correlate with DeviceFileEvents showing truncation operations. Alert on audit log gaps or deletions correlating with exploit-timing windows.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS Host/X-Forwarded-Host header poisoning attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'By exploiting the default permissive `trustedHosts` configuration, an attacker can poison the `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Host` header' but no UC specifically hunts for suspicious header values. Should detect mismatches between Host header and expected domain or repeated header-rewriting patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor resource-js endpoint requests for Host or X-Forwarded-Host values that deviate from registered domains, contain internal IPs, or include DNS rebinding patterns (same IP resolving to different internal names). Flag repeated header variations from same source within short window.

suggestion.title: JavaScript injection via baseUrl manipulation in Craft CMS responses
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection' via baseUrl manipulation causing '$baseUrl' to be controlled by attacker. No hunt checks response bodies for injected eval(), script tags, or onerror handlers referencing attacker-controlled baseUrl values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect resource-js endpoint responses (HTTP 200 + content-type:javascript) for eval() calls with non-constant arguments, script src attributes pointing to external/unusual domains, or window.baseUrl assignments with exfiltration callbacks. Correlate response content hash changes with unusual Host headers.

suggestion.title: Blind SSRF indicators from Craft CMS resource-js (DNS queries + timing patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Blind SSRF' vulnerability but UC_102_3 only monitors outbound IP traffic. Blind SSRF detection requires watching for DNS queries from web process during/after resource-js requests, HTTP timeout/error responses leaking internal structure, or unusual timing delays.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DNS resolution attempts from web processes (php-fpm, httpd, nginx) to internal IP ranges or reserved TLDs immediately following successful resource-js requests. Monitor for HTTP 5xx errors or timeouts in responses that may reveal internal IP/port information. Watch for multi-second request latencies that suggest blind SSRF probing.

suggestion.title: Session hijacking correlation with Craft CMS SSRF/header-poisoning chain
suggestion.rationale: MITRE technique T1185 (Browser Session Hijacking) is listed but no UC operationalizes it. Article describes attack chain leading to plugin installation; hijacked session would be necessary to authenticate those actions. Should detect cookie theft indicators or unusual session activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate resource-js requests with 200 status + JavaScript content-type to subsequent admin endpoint requests (e.g., /admin/plugins/install-plugin) from the SAME source IP but with DIFFERENT session cookie or User-Agent. Flag if admin requests occur immediately after reconnaissance/exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS trustedHosts bypass via localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 in Host header
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'default permissive `trustedHosts` configuration' is exploited. Attackers commonly bypass host validation by claiming to be localhost. Should detect resource-js requests with Host:127.0.0.1 or Host:localhost from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor resource-js endpoint for requests where Host or X-Forwarded-Host header contains localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, or [::1] but source IP is non-internal (not in RFC 1918 ranges). Single occurrence is suspicious; repeated attempts indicate active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Web shell upload/execution post-Craft CMS RCE
suggestion.rationale: UC_102_5 detects shell spawning but not subsequent web shell persistence. Article lists T1505.003 (Web Shell) as technique. Should monitor for file creation in web-accessible directories immediately after RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting web process spawning shell, monitor for new file creation in web root (e.g., /var/www/html, /var/www/craft/web) with PHP/JSP/ASPX extensions, or modification of existing files with suspicious inline code. Correlate file timestamps to shell execution timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can access the 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the core vulnerability. Pipeline failed to map the authentication-bypass vector to any detection. Need to flag HTTP requests to the sidecar endpoint that lack valid Splunk session credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically internal APIs like /services/sidecar/* or /api/sidecar/*) that originate from external/untrusted sources AND lack valid Splunk authentication cookies/tokens. Flag any requests that return HTTP 200/201 as exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations Initiated by Unauthenticated Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability 'could allow...create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the exploitation payload. Pipeline must detect file creation/truncation events that correlate with unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access. This closes the loop from initial access to impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation (or size-reduction) operations initiated by Splunk-owned processes (splunkd, sidecar-postgres, etc.) that target files outside $SPLUNK_HOME, especially system-critical paths or log directories. Cross-correlate with unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access logs from the prior use case to confirm exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Gap (Splunk Enterprise Patch Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides CVE-2026-20253 and federal patch due-date 2026-06-21. Pipeline should have generated a patch-status-tracking use case to identify unpatched instances at risk. Vulnerability scanner output is the detection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query your vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.) for instances of Splunk Enterprise flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 with patched_status = false or remediation_date > 2026-06-21. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify which instances are internet-facing or directly reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Port/Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint is network-accessible. Pipeline should detect the presence and network-accessibility of the sidecar service as a prerequisite to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exposed Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service ports (typically 8089-range or custom high-numbered ports used by Splunk sidecars). Alert if those ports are reachable from external IPs or DMZ-adjacent networks. Baseline internal-only access to the sidecar and flag cross-segment access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Rust Binary Execution and Network Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet 'Rebuilds in Rust'—Rust executables executing with outbound C2 connections is the core infection pattern. No detection UC provided despite explicit language identifying Rust as the malware implementation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with Rust toolchain signatures (cargo, rustc) or Rust runtime indicators in unexpected contexts. Correlate with anomalous outbound network connections on non-standard ports from system binaries or /tmp execution paths. Flag any Rust binary execution outside normal development workflows.

suggestion.title: Router Credential Harvesting and Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'routers and servers'—routers require credential compromise for botnet installation. Pipeline missed detection of router administrative access attempts, SSH key staging, or web UI authentication brute force patterns typical of router-focused botnets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed SSH/HTTP logins to routers (RFC 1918 addresses, common router gateways 192.168.1.1, 10.0.0.1) with credential patterns from known botnet wordlists. Detect repeated auth attempts followed by successful logins with new device fingerprints.

suggestion.title: DDoS Traffic Generation and Resource Exhaustion
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names DDoS as purpose ('for DDoS'). Pipeline has no detection UC for abnormal bandwidth consumption, packet flood patterns, or spoofed source IP traffic emanating from compromised routers/servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained outbound traffic spikes from routers/servers to previously unknown IPs, especially with identical packet sizes/TTLs suggesting flood tools. Flag sudden increases in DNS amplification queries or HTTP/TCP SYN flood patterns from single source to diverse targets.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence on Linux/Router Systems
suggestion.rationale: Botnet persistence on routers typically relies on cron jobs or init.d scripts (implicit from 'hijack routers' phrasing). No UC provided for cron job injection or suspicious scheduler modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on crontab modifications by non-root users, or cron jobs executing from /tmp or unusual paths. Detect repeated root cron job creation followed by process execution at predictable intervals. Monitor cron logs for suspicious binary execution patterns.

suggestion.title: C2 Domain/IP Infrastructure Beaconing and Callback Patterns
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted and no network-based detection UC. Botnet command-and-control is fundamental; article should provide C2 endpoints for detection of inbound/outbound callback traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS requests or IP connections to known RustDuck C2 infrastructure (pending IOC extraction). Detect regular callback traffic at fixed intervals from routers/servers to external IPs on non-standard ports. Flag encrypted traffic volumes inconsistent with normal router behavior.

suggestion.title: Binary Deployment and Lateral Propagation Across Router/Server Network Segments
suggestion.rationale: Article implies multi-target compromise ('routers and servers'). Pipeline missed detection of lateral movement patterns—file transfers between internal systems, worm-like propagation, or SSH key misuse for horizontal spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file writes to unusual locations (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) followed by execution from routers/servers. Monitor for SSH connections between router management interfaces and internal servers without administrative justification. Alert on identical binary deployment patterns across network devices in sequence.

suggestion.title: Monero Miner Process Execution on Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints'—the pipeline should detect spawning of xmrig, cryptonight, or known miner binaries with resource hijacking patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of known Monero miner tools (xmrig, cgminer variants) or process names matching miner signatures. Correlate with sustained high CPU/memory consumption (>80% CPU for >10min on application servers) and absence of legitimate batch jobs. High fidelity if Langflow processes spawn child processes executing miner code.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Langflow Public Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Langflow RCE Exploited'—pipeline should detect RCE attempts against Langflow endpoints (/api, /chat, /run routes) with payload indicators (bash, curl, wget, sh -c).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST/GET requests to Langflow endpoints containing command injection payloads (backticks, $(), pipe chains, /bin/sh). Alert on successful RCE (HTTP 200 + command output in response). Correlate with subsequent process creation under Langflow's UID.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution Under Langflow Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployment of miner via RCE—detection should capture when Langflow app server spawns unexpected child processes (sh, bash, python, curl) that then spawn miners or fetch payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent process is 'langflow' or 'python' (if Langflow runs under Python) and child process is /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or curl. Alert especially if child spawns a third-level child (e.g., bash → wget → xmrig). Establish baseline of legitimate Langflow child processes; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from Langflow to Miner Pool/C2
suggestion.rationale: Monero miner must connect to mining pool or C2 server to coordinate work—article implies network exfiltration via miner C2, should detect unusual outbound connections from app endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Langflow process or process running on Langflow endpoint host to known Monero mining pools (supportxmr.com, nanopool.org, 2miners.com IPs) or C2 IPs with Stratum protocol traffic patterns (port 3333, 14444, 9999 common for pools). Cross-reference against threat intel for miner C2.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion Anomaly on AI Application Servers
suggestion.rationale: Monero mining causes sustained resource consumption—'deployed' miner will generate CPU and memory anomalies on previously-clean Langflow endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when CPU utilization on Langflow/application hosts spikes to >75% sustained over 15+ min without corresponding legitimate workload (batch jobs, model inference). Pair with memory usage spike. Cross-correlate with network connections to mining pools and process creation logs to confirm miner presence.

suggestion.title: Parallel Process Execution from Distinct Parent Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'uncovering parallel threat activity'—two actors operating concurrently on same host. Pipeline missed detection of divergent process chains indicating multiple attack threads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation events showing multiple parent-child chains with distinct execution contexts, injected environments, or tool signatures occurring within tight timeframes on single host.

suggestion.title: Blended Tactics Defense Evasion Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'blended tactics conceal attacks and complicate detection'—defense evasion is the defining signature separating this intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate obfuscation, LOLBin abuse, and log-clearing events occurring in parallel from different processes or injection contexts to detect coordinated concealment.

suggestion.title: Multiple C2 Signatures from Single Intrusion
suggestion.rationale: 'Parallel threat activity' implies concurrent command channels. Two actors require distinct or overlapping C2 infrastructure requiring concurrent traffic detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple distinct user agents, timing cadences, or encryption signatures in outbound traffic from same host, correlating to separate C2 infrastructure per actor.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Divergent Credential Sets
suggestion.rationale: Dual actors post-intrusion suggest independent objectives and lateral movement to distinct targets. Article's 'uncovering' phrasing indicates forensic recovery of separate movement patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pass-the-hash or RDP/WinRM activity using distinct stolen credentials targeting different subnets or asset types, segregated by timing or process origin.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Channel Divergence Between Actors
suggestion.rationale: Dual actors typically target separate data or use separate exfil infrastructure. 'Uncovering parallel' implies distinct and separately detectable data theft patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple distinct outbound data transfers with different tool signatures, encryption methods, or destination endpoints, each correlating to separate actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Targeting Multiple Account Sets
suggestion.rationale: Two actors in one intrusion implies separate credential acquisition. Article subtitle 'uncovering' suggests both actors' credential-theft activities are forensically recoverable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on credential spray or brute-force attacks using distinct user agent strings, source process images, or injection contexts, revealing multiple concurrent credential-theft operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct exploitation vector with zero detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (standard ports 8191 or variant) without authentication headers or TLS mutual auth. Flag non-SSL or missing Authorization header on POST/GET to /services, /sidecar, or /postgres paths.

suggestion.title: Detect File Creation/Truncation Originating from Splunk Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—no rule exists for this post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events from Splunk Enterprise service process (splunk user, splunkd) outside scheduled maintenance windows. Cross-reference against Splunk asset inventory to confirm unexpected file-system modifications.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset-exposure baseline; article provides CVE identifier but pipeline omitted inventory/scanning directive entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances on vulnerable version range for CVE-2026-20253. Validate patch deployment status against federal due date 2026-06-21. Flag any unpatched instances with network-level ingress from untrusted segments.

suggestion.title: Detect Internet-Exposed Splunk Services with Missing Authentication
suggestion.rationale: T1190 exploitation context requires external-facing service detection; article emphasizes public-facing application vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk Enterprise services reachable from WAN/internet. Flag any with unauthenticated access enabled or PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint exposed without reverse-proxy authentication controls.

suggestion.title: Monitor PostgreSQL Sidecar Service for Unauthorized Database-Level File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector isolated to PostgreSQL sidecar—requires database-level monitoring absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service logs for unauthenticated connection attempts or SQL statements that invoke file-system operations (COPY, CREATE TEMP, shell commands via postgres extensions). Alert on any without valid service account credentials.

suggestion.title: Hunt for CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Signatures
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV = active exploitation observed; pipeline must include in-flight attack detection; article specifies no signature patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index Splunk access logs and WAF telemetry for requests matching known CVE-2026-20253 payloads: path traversal attempts (../, ..\ in sidecar paths), SQL injection syntax, unauthenticated POST to critical endpoints. Trigger alerts on first detection per source IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Sidecar PostgreSQL Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct indicator of exploitation pathway. This is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service (typically port 5432 or custom sidecar port) originating from untrusted networks or lacking authentication headers. Alert on successful connection establishment without prior Splunk auth tokens or session identifiers.

suggestion.title: Splunk File Truncation via Unauthenticated Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies capability to 'truncate arbitrary files'—direct impact indicator. Detection requires monitoring file-destruction events on Splunk infrastructure correlated with sidecar service access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk process spawning file deletion or truncation syscalls (unlink, truncate) on critical config/data directories. Correlate with prior unauthenticated network access to sidecar endpoint. Alert if file ops occur outside normal Splunk maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Port Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes endpoint access as vulnerability surface—exposure scan IOC. Organizations must identify exposed sidecar ports to understand blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for externally accessible Splunk Enterprise instances exposing sidecar service ports. Use port banner grabbing or known sidecar query patterns to identify exposed instances. Cross-reference against asset inventory to find unexpected external-facing Splunk boxes.

suggestion.title: File Creation via Unauthenticated Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file creation is equally exploitable for malware staging or credential dumps. Separate from truncation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation events on Splunk infrastructure originating from sidecar processes, especially in unexpected paths (/tmp, system directories, web-accessible locations). Correlate with prior unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Version Inventory & CVE Match
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Splunk Enterprise' as vulnerable product. Standard asset-exposure hunt requires identifying affected versions and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management DB and vulnerability scanner output for Splunk Enterprise instances. Match against known-vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-20253. Alert on unpatched instances published after federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV implies 'currently being exploited' and federal due-date remediation; standard asset-exposure hunt is canonical for this class. Cite: 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal "Known Exploited Vulnerabilities" catalog only adds CVEs that have been **observed exploited in the wild**.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances exposed to public or untrusted networks. Enumerate open TCP ports on known Splunk services (default 8089, 8000, 8088). Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scan results. Prioritize instances with patch lag >7 days from federal due-date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline should detect requests to this endpoint without valid authentication context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/PUT requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically `/services/server/control/restart` or sidecar-specific paths documented in Splunk advisories) where HTTP response indicates unauthenticated access (401 → success pattern anomaly, or 200 without authentication header). Track file-creation/truncation payloads in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations from Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Missing use case for file-system events initiated by sidecar process outside normal operational patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create/write/truncate events originating from Splunk sidecar process (e.g., `postgres_sidecar.exe`, `splunkd` sub-process) targeting arbitrary paths outside Splunk installation directory, especially system files, logs, or authentication databases. Baseline normal file operations and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Fingerprinting & Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the vulnerable surface. Attackers will probe for this service; detection should capture reconnaissance. Cite: attack requires locating and accessing the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify scanning/probing of common PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths (e.g., `/sidecar/`, `/postgres/`, vendor-specific control paths) in HTTP logs. Flag multiple failed connection attempts followed by successful unauthenticated access, or GET requests probing for service existence without valid auth headers.

suggestion.title: Splunk Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability class: 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Detect attempts to invoke critical functions (file operations, service control) without proper authentication. Article: 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for failed authentication events followed by successful critical-function invocations (file create, file delete, config write) within same session. Flag requests to authenticated-only endpoints (identified via Splunk documentation) that succeed without valid session token or Bearer auth header.

suggestion.title: Log Tampering / Deletion via CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation indicator: attackers exploiting file-truncation capability to destroy evidence. Cite: 'truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden truncation or deletion of audit logs, event logs, or forensic data following successful unauthorized access to sidecar endpoint. Correlate file-deletion events with prior unauthenticated HTTP requests. Flag rapid bulk-delete patterns from sidecar-related processes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entries target 'exposed assets' currently being exploited in the wild; canonical asset-exposure hunt is mandatory for any internet-facing Splunk instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with public IPs or non-RFC1918 routing. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-21 sets remediation urgency.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct exploitation mechanism, not post-compromise behavior.
